editorial:
Imagine you are tagging along with a friend to film a documentary about his long-lost sister. You end up at Eden Parish, a hidden village where everyone seems way too happy and polite. The vibe is super creepy because the leader, Father, treats everyone like family while keeping them away from the outside world. You will feel that slow build of tension as you realize that this perfect little town is actually a trap. It feels like you are right there with the camera crew, watching the red flags pop up one by one until things go completely wrong.

The acting is great, and the way it is filmed makes it feel like a real found-footage movie. It does start off a bit slow, but the ending is a wild ride that will leave you shocked. If you like stories about cults and secret societies, you will love this.
endingExplained: Everything ends in a bloodbath when Father tells his followers it is time to leave the earth. He convinces everyone to drink a poisoned drink so they can go to heaven together. The journalists try to escape, but they are hunted down by the cult members. In the end, almost everyone dies from the poison or is killed, leaving the village as a silent graveyard of people who trusted the wrong man.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves found-footage movies and scary stories about cults.
